subject.title: fix: prevent channel allowlists from granting owner access

question: Should this security fix preserve trusted context owner overrides and the shipped explicit owner-wildcard behavior, or intentionally remove either authority path as a breaking hardening change?
rationale: The cross-channel escalation must be fixed, but the PR also changes established configuration and plugin-context authorization contracts; only maintainers can approve those additional security and upgrade semantics.

options.title: Narrow the fix
options.body: Keep trusted context owners and explicit owner wildcards working, while removing only channel-allowlist fallback from `senderIsOwner`.

options.title: Adopt strict explicit identities
options.body: Remove wildcard and context-derived owner authority only with an approved migration, updated contracts, fresh-install and upgrade tests, and operator-facing recovery guidance.

options.title: Pause the patch
options.body: Hold this PR until the permanent owner-authority contract is decided and then implement the security fix against that contract.

recommendation.title: Narrow the fix
recommendation.body: Keep trusted context owners and explicit owner wildcards working, while removing only channel-allowlist fallback from `senderIsOwner`.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated ownership of the shared command authorization and sender-identity architecture.
